text:
maya: Heads-up — bringing up draft-model-v4-int8 for inference. Want a short checklist for speculative decoding + quant onboarding. Goal: confirm we don't regress quality while getting ~1.8-2.2x decode speed improvement.
owen: Nice. Primary constraints: KV cache size, kernel fallback for int8, and batch sizing. Also routing policy for hosted vs dedicated.
liam: For evals, we should separate macro benchmarks (LM score, ppl) from downstream suites (QA, summarization, instruction-following). Speculative decoding can change token-level distribution even if end-task accuracy is similar.
sara: Quick checklist I keep:
- baseline run (fp16) on same traces
- int8 decode perf + memory
- speculative configs (spec p, draft length thresholds)
- per-token logprob drift
- hallucination/regression sampling on instruction set
- latency tail (p95/p99)
maya: + add eval harness commands please, I can run on infra sandbox.
owen: Use this harness snippet:
```
./run_eval.sh --model draft-model-v4-int8 --mode compare --baseline draft-model-v4-fp16 \
  --workloads qa,summarize,chat --spec-params "p=0.9,max_drafts=2,early_accept=0.6" \
  --batch-config small
```
liam: Also log token-level KL divergence vs baseline for generations. If KL > 0.15 on average in core prompt sets, flag for manual review.
sara: Eval-bot ran quick sims last night, attached summary:
- throughput: 2.05x vs fp16 (batch=8, seq=1024)
- avg latency: 0.54x (per token)
- p95 latency: 1.1x (speculative stalls on rare long contexts)
- instr-follow accuracy (instruction-suite v2): -0.8% absolute
- rouge/summ: -0.4 F1
- hallucination rate (fact-check set): +1.6% false claims
eval-bot: NOTE: sample payloads and seeds stored at s3://redwood-evals/draft-v4/int8/spec-2026-03-18
maya: The hallucination uptick worries me. Possible causes: quantization + speculative accept threshold too permissive.
owen: Agreed. Two quick mitigations to try:
1) tighten `early_accept` to 0.7 and re-run
2) enable conservative fallback: if draft avg logprob < baseline avg - 0.8, regenerate without spec
liam: For measurement we must add per-token logprob moving average and a per-response acceptance trace. That helps spot where spec accepts a low-quality draft early.
sara: Also run sensitivity sweep for temperature (0.0,0.2,0.5) since spec interacts with sampling temp.
maya: Action items:
- owen: spin a small dedicated job with int8 kernels + spec p sweep (due EOD)
- liam: add KL/acceptance traces to eval harness and push PR to repo
- sara: run full instruction-suite + hallucination benchmark after owen's run
- maya: coordinate results and decide rollback vs tuned deploy
owen: I can start the job. Using node g5-8x for parity. Will tag results with metadata `spec-early0.6/0.7/0.8`.
sara: If we need, we can also test 4-bit quant with outlier-clipping as alternative — might recover hallucination without full fp16 cost.
liam: Note on reporting: include seed, prompt id, and top draft acceptance step so we can reproduce the exact decision boundary.
maya: Thanks. If we see continued regression >1% instr-follow or >2% hallucination, we'll block for canary.
eval-bot: Quick log extract (example failed case):
```
> prompt_id: 4729
> baseline: "...Paris is the capital of France." (logprob -1.2)
> int8+spec accepted draft at step 6: "...Paris is the capital of Spain." (avg logprob -0.9)
> accept_reason: early_accept threshold passed
```
owen: Oof — that's the kind of story we want to avoid. I'll add the logprob delta check.
sara: For the run matrix, I recommend columns: spec_p, early_accept, temp, quant_mode, batch, p95_latency, instr_acc, halluc_rate, notes
maya: OK I'll wait for owen's job and liam's harness patch. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
liam: PR link when ready — i'll tag you both.
owen: Started job at 1803054500, ETA ~2h. Posting link when done.
maya: Appreciated. We'll reconvene after results and decide rollout path.
